question: Why is even immense material wealth insufficient compared to possessing this kaula knowledge?
premises: One may have an accumulation vast enough to fill the ocean with jewels
Such wealth is being contrasted with the value of the teaching
inference: Even immeasurable wealth is inferior to the kaula teaching
uncertainties: The form akretuṃ is obscure and may be a textual corruption
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels.
